The following demonstrates some simple features of `julia` combined with `jupyter`.

# How to generate this output
Produce a PDF file with this script, using the following `bash` invocation.
```bash
quarto render test.qmd --to=pdf --from=markdown+tex_math_single_backslash
```
Note the untidy `--from=markdown+tex_math_single_backslash` parameter,
required to avoid use of the unsophisticated `$` and `$$` switches.

# Loading data
After `jupyter` has invoked `julia`, load `RDatasets.jl`, capture `iris` data, display \(6\) rows.

```{julia}
    using RDatasets
    iris = dataset("datasets", "iris") ;
    first(iris, 6)
```

# A simple plot
Now load `Gadfly.jl` and plot a test image in @fig-test.
```{julia}
#| label: fig-test
#| fig-cap: "Test image"
    using Gadfly
    p = plot(iris, x=:SepalLength, y=:SepalWidth, Geom.point)
```
